utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. Before I invite Mr. Zecevic to resume his cross-examination, could we have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Crispian Smith, case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic appearing for the Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence this afternoon, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I would remind you that you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, good day. Yesterday we stopped when dealing with 1D001361, tab 72. This document is a report on implementation, dated the 19th of June, 1992, forwarded by your chief of the department, Zoran Josic. I see we don't have it up on the screen yet. 1D001361.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has to do with bringing in three individuals, in fact, it's not an implementation: Savic, Miroljub; Krajisnik, Dragan; Miljkovic, Milan, on the 17th of July, 1992. Can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These three individuals, if you have a look at their names, would appear to be Serbs. That's the conclusion one could draw?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A criminal report was attached to the document for the crime of robbery, in which Nezirevic, Irfan, from Banja Luka was the injured party, and 1.500 dinars was stolen from that individual. Can you see that on the first page in the statement of reasons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The rest of the document has to do with documents that were attached to the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That is evidence in support of the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If there are no objections, I would suggest that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D207, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, just one other question in relation to the document that has been admitted. Mr. Irfan Nezirevic, from Banja Luka, is of Muslim ethnicity; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the first name and last name, he should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm afraid it's my fault. I was slightly distracted. I don't know that -- is this a document the witness said he saw? Because if not, shouldn't it be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I posed the question, Ms. Korner, this is the document which was signed by his --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, right. I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It comes from the SJB Banja Luka. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please have a look at document under tab 100. 1D031872 is the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I won't be tendering this document. All I would like to do is ask you the following: On page 2 of the document, there's a letter from the Public Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka, dated the 22nd of July, 1992. The deputy public prosecutor, Enver Kerenovic, has signed the document. Are you familiar -- or, rather, do you know Enver Kerenovic, the deputy public Prosecutor in the Banja Luka Public Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the name, but I don't know the person personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct to say that this is a person of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the first and last name, that should be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, in the Public Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka and in the Court -- the First Instance Court in Banja Luka, and in the higher-level organs, higher-level courts, Prosecutor's Office, do you know how many individuals were employed in those bodies of Muslim ethnicity in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that one of the investigative judges was of Muslim ethnicity, Mirsad -- well, it slipped my mind now, the name. Can you remember it, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Krgovic will be able to remind you of that person's exact name. Please have a look at document 101 -- under tab 101. 1D011037 is the number of the document, tab 101.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a letter from the Banja Luka CSB, forwarded to all the SJBs in the area, signed by the chief of the sector, the head of the sector, Djuro Bulic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a letter in which information is provided to all SJBs about the events -- or the event that took place when unidentified individuals opened fire on religion facilities, on a monastery and a church in Bosanski Aleksandrovac, and the bishopric in Banja Luka informed the CSB of this event. Do you remember this event?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this event, but I can see, on the basis of the contents of the document, that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having ever received this letter?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But since it was forwarded to the Public Security Station, so all the SJBs in the area, it must certainly have been forwarded to the Banja Luka SJB as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no reason for that not to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 2 says that the head of the sector says that it's obvious that there are attacks on religious facilities and other -- and at other places in the area, and he issues instructions according to which it's necessary to take measures in order to prevent such occurrences and in order to identify the perpetrators of the acts reported so far. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As part of your responsibilities in the Banja Luka SJB, did you take any steps and measures in order to prevent religious facilities, religious buildings, from being attacked, and did you take measures to identify perpetrators of crimes that had been reported at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly acted in accordance with this letter, and at meetings we conveyed the orders issued. The police stations in the area of the Banja Luka Police Station received this. They would receive this letter at the same time that I would receive it in the headquarters. They would receive it, and naturally they would have to abide by the instructions in the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, I suggest that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's now have a look at tab 102. 1D031955 is the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on arresting and remanding in custody certain individuals. The 1st of August, 1992, is the date. It was sent from the SJB in Banja Luka and signed by your head of the sector, Mr. Zoran Josic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this report was sent to the Public Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a report --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. We don't have the document up on the screen in the e-court system. 1D031955. That's the document that we commented on just a minute ago. I interrupted you when you started answering my question. I said that this was a document that was sent to the Public Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka. It's a report on arresting and remanding in custody a certain individual. You said, Yes, that's a report, and then I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a report on arresting and taking into custody a certain individual who was to be placed in detention. That's what it says in the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 2 of this document, we have a criminal report on the basis of which we can see that the Marjan Pranjic, a Croat by ethnicity, was detained, and criminal proceedings were instituted against him because there were reasonable grounds to suspect that on the 31st of July, 1992, he used fire-arms and a hunting rifle, a 60-millimetre calibre, he used this to kill Kosic, Ivica, born in 1966 in Banja Luka; can you see this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ivica Kosic seems to be a Croat, if we judge by his name. That's the injured party?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could draw the conclusion that he is a Croat by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In fact, the bit you're reading is not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The bit you're reading is actually not being shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not -- I don't follow you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Part of the document you were reading is not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I said page 2 of the document. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In English, it's not -- it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It should be the previous page in English. I'm sorry. Yes, this is the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the document, which shows that he was suspected of having killed Mr. Ivica Kozic, born in 1966, from Banja Luka. And you confirmed that the injured party is probably a Croat; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, as this is a document from the Banja Luka SJB, it's a criminal report, and there's a report and attached documents, so if there are no objections to this request, I suggest that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I'm a little bit lost here. Can you remind me what tab number this is in your binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 102, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 102, 102. That would be number 1D001955?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. There's something wrong with your list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could you assist me by telling me on a thumbnail -- although like the previous two documents, there being no objection, I ordered them admitted and marked, to what end are these documents being exhibited? As I said, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the allegation from the Prosecution side is that during the relevant period in the indictment, the MUP of Republika Srpska was conducting sham inquiries and were not prosecuting people or filing criminal reports and criminal complaints to the courts on perpetrators of crimes against non-Serbs. Now, what I'm trying to establish over here is not -- is that the -- and which the witness confirmed, basically, at the very beginning, that the SJB Banja Luka, which he was heading, was, in fact, doing everything in accordance with the law, protecting all citizens despite their nationality, who the victim are, or who the perpetrator are, and that is the purpose why I am going through this exercise, Your Honours. I think it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And in support of this, you propose to tender how many documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have, actually, one more document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. This would be Exhibit 1D209, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said to the Trial Chamber, please have a look at document 107. 1D010044 is the document number. This is also a report on arresting and remanding an individual in custody. It's dated the 19th of August, 1992, forwarded by the Banja Luka SJB, the head of the sector -- your head of the sector, Zoran Josic, signed the document, and it concerns arresting a certain Selvir Zilic, whose mother's name is Fatima, probably, from Banja Luka. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Zilic, Selvir, is a Roma by ethnicity, but of Muslim faith; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the criminal report, it says he's a Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the second page of this report, there's a description of the crime, and it says that he is responsible for having committed the crime of murder. When engaged in a verbal conflict, he killed someone by throwing a hand-grenade on Saban Ramadan. He threw a hand-grenade at Saban Ramadan. It's the fourth page in the English. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Attached to this criminal report are the documents which are part of this criminal report. And if there are no objections, I tender this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D210.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I have now three documents which I wish to show you. But prior to that, I have to put a question to you. It is true that every citizen can file an oral criminal report by coming to a public security station and telling the officer on duty about the event, and thereby filing an oral criminal report; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the law, every citizen who learns of a crime is duty-bound to report it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That naturally includes the injured party; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I would like to show you document 111, which is 1D002029. Again, this is a document from your SJB. It's your tab 111. This document was signed by the chief of department, Zoran Josic. It was sent on the 8th of September, 1992, to the Public Prosecutor's Office. And it says there that this was a report on the oral criminal report filed by Suljo Dujma due to an attempted murder. And as you will see on the next page, it says that he was stopped by three uniformed persons, who fired on the back of the car in which he was driving. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Suljo Dujma, according to the first and last name, should be of Muslim ethnicity; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say so. He could also be a Roma of Muslim faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, he's not a Serb?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Another example of this type of verbal criminal report can be found in tab 82; 1D001828, tab 82. This is a report on an oral criminal report which was filed. The document is signed by your head of department, Zoran Josic. The date is 15th of July, 1992. And on the second page of this document - could we please turn to the next page - we have a record on an oral criminal report that was filed, and it says there that citizen Ismet Zilkic, born in Zavidovici, and residing in Banja Luka, filed a criminal report against an unidentified person due to a crime of robbery. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll put a similar question to you. Ismet Zilkic should be of Muslim ethnicity; right? At any rate, he's not a Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Notwithstanding my slight confusion about a written record of an oral report, continue, Mr. Zecevic. That was an aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please turn to tab 87, which is the next document; 1D006703, tab 87. In order to assist the Trial Chamber to understand the procedure as it existed, let us look at this. When an injured party or any other citizen comes in to file an oral criminal report, that person would go to a person on duty at the Public Security Station or at the police station; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would just need to come to any police institution and he would be sent to the right place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "he would be sent to the right place," you mean that this person would be sent to one of the inspectors, who then compiles a written record on an oral criminal report that was received, and in that criminal record he will write down whatever that person who came to the police station said to him; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And following that, that written record, which is taken down by a police officer, is sent to the relevant public prosecutor, in this form that we just saw, for the public prosecutor to act upon it; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us return to this document. Again, this is dated 13th of July, 1992, sent to the Public Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka by your chief of department, Mr. Zoran Josic. This is a written record of a criminal report filed by Ivan Pranjic due to aggravated theft; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on the second page, we have this written record compiled by an authorised official, and in the left lower corner we see the person who made this oral report, and that person signed this written record; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on this written record, we can see that Pranjic, Ivan, father's name Anto, born in 1937, a taxi-driver by occupation, filed a criminal report against three persons wearing a camouflage uniform who asked money from him, entered his house -- or forced him to take them into his house, and from there they confiscated from him 12.000 Austrian shillings, 1.500 Swiss francs and $90 US. Do you see the amounts here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ivan Pranjic, father's name Anto, should be of Croat ethnicity; that's how it looks, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I thought you had only one more --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, one more criminal file. Those are just to show that there was a possibility to file the oral criminal reports, because that's -- that was one of the options available to the citizens in accordance with the law. And I'm moving on from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate it. I appreciate your patience. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, please, for the sake of illustration, let us show to the Trial Chamber three groups of documents out of which we shall comment upon just one or two documents in each group. Can we please see 118, which is 1D031857, tab 118. Mr. Tutus, isn't it a fact that CSB Banja Luka provided so-called forensic services by providing their forensic technicians to all other institutions in the territory under their jurisdiction; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were the only one who had such expertise and forensic equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now that we've mentioned forensic expertise and equipment, let us clarify that. This includes finger-printing expertise, establishing someone's identity based on their finger-prints; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, various types of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Including analysis of fire-arms and explosives; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, including that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Analysis of gunpowder particles, which is popularly known as paraffin glove?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in all police stations in the territory of CSB Banja Luka, in cases where they needed to establish the identity of the perpetrator or various elements of the crime committed, these police stations would send their request -- would send a letter to the CSB requesting their help or their services in conducting this forensic analysis; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at this document. It's dated 14th of August, 1992. It requires finger-print analysis, expert analysis. And in the body of the text, we see that they require that an analysis of finger-prints be conducted, finger-prints found after the murders of Zlata Vandi, Bozidar Jovic and Ante Lipovac at the Romantika Restaurant?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the chief of the department, Milorad Djuric?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Milorad Djuric. I'm familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He was --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was chief of Crime Prevention Department or Sector. I'm not sure whether it was "Department" or "Sector," and it was within the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the persons who were killed, the victims, Vandi, Jovic and Lipovac, were of Croat ethnicity; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by their names and last names, they could be of Croat ethnicity, but I'm not familiar with this particular case. I don't know the details of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at page 2, which is a request for expert forensic analysis which was sent to the CSB; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where we see the signature of Milorad Djuric, they're actually informing us about the results of this expert forensic analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But on the next page, on page 2, we see your request sent to them for the finger-print forensic analysis that they are informing you of?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was -- this is signed by Nedzad Jusufovic. Is this what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzad Jusufovic used to work at the centre, and in the heading it says "Sector for Forensic Analysis" and "KDZ." This is within the CSB. Now, whether they use this particular form, I wouldn't really be able to tell you. It's possible that the CSB acted in this case throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Chief of department, Nedzad Jusufovic, the name you just recognised, who worked at the centre, is of Muslim ethnicity; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he used to work at the Banja Luka CSB in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was chief of Forensic Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, given that I brought these documents to your attention, I don't know whether I should now tender them into evidence. And I have a group of almost identical documents which all speak of the same subject, a finger-print forensic analysis, so I'm not sure whether the Trial Chamber would accept my suggestion which I stated -- which I gave before starting with cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: How many documents are we talking about, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in relation to finger-printing analysis, I have five more documents in addition to this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, sorry, but I'm not sure that -- again, how this can go in through this witness, who doesn't know anything about the documents at all and has never seen them before. And as I understand it, as he told us earlier, he knows nothing about crime -- the Crime Prevention Department or whatever it's called. I mean, I have no -- I have no objection to it being MFI'd until a more suitable witness can deal with them and the whole group, as such, but not admitted as evidence for the moment, on the basis of the rules, as they now stand, about how documents come in. If there's a complete change, then it's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do have some documents here which come directly from the Banja Luka Public Security Station. It was because of time constraints that I did not wish to go document by document and ask that those documents which came from elsewhere be MFI'd, whereas those documents which came from the SJB to be admitted, though I have to say that I don't mind if the documents, as such, are only MFI'd for the time being and then we may eventually ask for them to be tendered into evidence through a different witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Ms. Korner, before we rule, is there -- although Mr. Zecevic hasn't used this phrase, is there a problem, in terms of your reservation, with the documents -- with the witness being seen as someone who can testify to the system, methods, and practice?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, because the witness, himself, doesn't actually deal with any of this, doesn't know about this, and, indeed, in terms said, when he was giving evidence-in-chief, that he didn't know how any of this worked. Your Honours, we're back to the same old problem, and the reason I'm raising this objection is twofold. One is, as my understanding, these are not documents that come from our CSB collection. There's no sign of that. And, Your Honour, I have reservations at the moment, without a statement, as I've indicated, from whoever provided these documents from the Defence, that they are authentic documents which come from the CSB. That's my first reservation. The second reservation is that if Your Honours, as we've discussed, want documents to come in through witnesses who can speak to them, then this witness can't really speak to them. The criminal reports, we will, in fact, be calling witnesses with whom -- who can deal with those. These, I don't know about, and that's my reservation. If we change the policy, and subject to relevance and authenticity, it's not necessary to have a witness speak to them, that's fine. But at the moment, it seems that if we're having this difficulty getting our documents in because we have to go through these hoops, then the same should apply to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, in considering your application to have these documents admitted, there are two questions which we don't think we've heard evidence about. One is the provenance of the documents, and, building on what Ms. Korner has raised, the authenticity. But we aren't sure that the testimony of the witness so far has confirmed a familiarity with the system or the type of documents or the procedures. So if we could have some greater assistance on those two points, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in relation to the first question, I think that I spoke about this yesterday, about the source -- the provenance of documents. They originate from the Office for Investigations into War Crimes of Republika Srpska. I affirm again that the OTP must be in possession of these documents because they are filed in the archives of the CSB Banja Luka. However, if the OTP continues to deny this, we will have to ultimately call a witness who will confirm that, indeed, back in 1998 KFOR came into possession of these documents and forwarded them to the Prosecution. This will only amount to a waste of time. Still, I think that as far as the Defence is concerned, it will be an exercise to confirm the authenticity of the documents. As for the latter question of Their Honours, I will ask the witness to explain the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I asked you if you were familiar with the fact that the Security Services Centre was the only agency which had a forensic department and the necessary technology for forensic examination across the territory covered by the CSB, and your answer was in the affirmative?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The Banja Luka Public Security Station did not have any forensic staff or technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Throughout your term of office as chief of the Public Security Station Banja Luka, had you ever used the services of the Forensic Department of the Banja Luka CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used their services throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain the procedure involved?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that a murder takes place, or a crime such as a burglary, and a crime scene team would attend the scene together with the investigating judge and sometimes with the prosecutor, himself. Technicians would preserve any trace evidence found at the scene. Normally, artifacts would be recovered, such as the ones used for forced break and entry or for murder. The traces are preserved, photographs are made, the evidence is lifted, and then a request is forwarded to the Forensics Department to engage in any forensic analysis that may be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the screen, you can see one such form which is, in fact, a request for forensic analysis. Is this the sort of request you would be sending to the CSB when you required the assistance of their forensic technicians?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't our request. This is, in fact, the response from the Forensics Department to our request. So what we are looking at is not a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 2 -- this is page 2. So I know this isn't your request. You've explained this. My question is: You, as the Public Security Station, did you send similar requests, requests with similar contents, to the CSB whenever you required forensic analyses?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we now turn to page 5 of the document. This is the same document 118, page 5, where we have a criminal report. The criminal report bears the date of the 17th of August, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if you are continuing to lead evidence from the witness to answer the second question that we posed, we are satisfied on that aspect, and our ruling is that the documents may be marked for identification not pending a further witness coming in to prove them, but pending the matter of the authenticity being resolved at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we're satisfied with the questions and what we have heard from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. And may I inquire, also, does it refer to the whole set of the documents or just this particular document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: This was the whole set -- the whole set, because I think the understanding was that we would use a specimen in each case and operate on the assumption that the specimen accurately represents the bulk. Or should it turn out not to be so, we're going to have to decide what to do about that. But we will operate on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have six documents altogether that would need to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Therefore, the documents will be Exhibits 1D214 through 1D219, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If it assists on the first matter, in order for us not to have to keep getting up and saying, Where do the documents come from, and so on and so forth, if the Defence are prepared to provide us with statements from people saying either this comes from the Banja Luka CSB or from General Praljak's web site, or wherever it is, then at least we know where we are, and then we can make our own inquiries. It's as simple as that, and that, I think, will save a lot of time in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The tab -- or the first document is 118, and the other ones?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will read the documents. The first document is tab 118, document 1D031857. The next document is tab 92, document 1D005936. The next document is tab 91, 1D006090. The next document is tab 90, and the number is 1D006095. And the next document is tab 86, 1D005940. And the last document is tab 81, 1D030457.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can we have a look now at document -- this is a document from a different batch which concerns the analysis of firearms, behind tab 71, 1D031845. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 19th of June, 1992. This is a report on the findings of a ballistic analysis of fire-arms in connection with the killing of Admir Selimovic from Sanica, which took place on the 27th of April, 1992, where the chief of department, Milorad Djuric, the same person we talked about before, is sending this report to the Public Security Station in Kljuc; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The subject involved is the ballistic analysis of the fire-arms, and Admir Selimovic is presumably, judging by his name, a Muslim, is he not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just as you've confirmed before, as the Banja Luka Public Security Station, you, just as is the case with the Kljuc Public Security Station, sent to the CSB Forensics Department any requests for ballistic analysis of fire-arms involved in certain cases; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the procedure was identical to the one we referred to on the issue of finger-printing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope that there is no need for us to examine this any further. I have 13 documents from this category, from this batch. And if we are in agreement, can these documents be equally MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I really think no. I mean, Banja Luka, fine. Kljuc, and I don't know how many other different security stations, you have ample opportunity to call real evidence about this and not put them in through this witness. So these I object to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Korner obviously hasn't understood this. These are documents from the Banja Luka CSB, from their Forensics Department that was involved in forensic analysis for the entire territory of Krajina, the entire area covered by the CSB, and it concerned all cases. It was done for all cases and for all SJBs. So these are documents from the CSB in Banja Luka, and they have to do with certain murders throughout the territory of Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I do understand that. What I'm now saying is that there are proper witnesses the Defence can -- they could have been put in to any other witness -- well, actually, we haven't called anyone from Kljuc, it's fair to say, but they must be put in through people who can talk to the circumstances, if it's at all possible. And where it's possible -- and I haven't checked the rest, but if it's going to other places like Sanski Most and the like, then people -- it should be put to witnesses who have knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, Ms. Korner, if I -- well, first of all, could you assist me? Is your objection to the attempt to mark the entire batch according to specimen or is it that this witness -- or is it that this witness cannot speak to the documents? Because if it is the latter, as I understand the evidence led and the purpose for which they are being -- the documents are being put in, is again to illustrate what had gone on, as contrasted with the truth or accuracy of the contents of the complaint. And, again, having regard to what we know about this witness's competence to speak authoritatively to the systems and methods that existed in the time, hasn't the Defence met the necessary crossing threshold for so admitting the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if they're being put in purely for system, but I don't think that's why they are being put in. They are being put in as to the truth of the contents, which is, namely, that an investigation was taking place in respect of each of these individual reports that are being put in. That's what I understand Mr. Zecevic to be saying. I think he's nodding. It's not just system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps I over-simplified the matter. Clearly, it is beyond system, but as I understand it, Mr. Zecevic is still on that plank in his platform that notwithstanding the thesis of the Prosecution about the discrimination, for want of a better word, in the investigation of complaints, that, in fact, investigations were done by the book, was the expression --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely, that's what he was trying to prove. I absolutely agree with that. And as I say, he doesn't have to prove it; he's trying to raise a doubt as to any Prosecution theory. But that's my objection, Your Honour. If these are being put in and Your Honours are going to be asked to accept them as evidence of the truth of the contents, that it appears, on the face of it, a full investigation was taking place into various aspects, then it is, with respect, not the witness to whom these documents should go in. It should be a witness who can speak to these investigations. That's the basis of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, we're back to the same issue that we were in relation to the previous batch of documents that we admitted MFI; namely, the question that relates to the witness's knowledge of the forensic investigations done by the CSB in respect of fire-arms. And we were looking for the evidence offered by the witness, but I just couldn't find it in my quick search. So maybe the easiest thing is simply if you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I asked the witness -- I asked the witness, Your Honour, during -- previously, I asked the witness if the requests, such as these, for the forensic analysis of the fire-arms have been sent by his station, and was it done according to the same procedure which applied to the finger-tip forensic investigation, and he confirmed. And I thought that that was enough. I can give you the reference, Your Honour, if you'll bear with me just -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So what you're saying is, basically, that forensic analysis of finger-prints and forensic analysis of bullets from fire-arms is basically the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the procedure is completely the same, because the CSB Banja Luka had the resources, had the necessary equipment, for conducting these forensic investigations, and they did that for the whole territory of the CSB Banja Luka, for all stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: For the same reasons that we marked the previous batch for identification, this batch is, according to the specimen, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let me -- may I read first the tab numbers and the documents? Thank you. So the first document is tab 71, 1D031845. The next document is tab 110, 1D005259. The next document is tab 75, 1D002181. The next document is 74 -- tab 74, 1D005924. The next document is tab 69, 1D004793. Then the next document is tab 85, 1D001845. The next document is tab 78, 1D006652. The next document is tab 103, 1D005900. The next document is tab 98, 1D001903. The next document is tab 97, 1D031951. The next document is tab 99, 1D005944. The next document is tab 95, 1D001874. And the last document is tab 112, document 1D0027 -- 2073.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those will be Exhibits 1D220 through 1D232, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, which conveniently brings us to the point at which we take the break. So we'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness comes back in again and Mr. Zecevic continues, can I just bring to your attention one matter which VWS has brought to our attention? Apparently, Mr. Tutus asked them whether, over the weekend, he could have copies of the transcripts of his testimony. Well, my first reaction was, well, it's an unusual request, but given that he's testified publicly and, in theory, it should be on the internet ASAP, which in reality it isn't, we couldn't stop him if he wanted to do that. However, the point made by Mr. Zecevic just a moment ago is actually a good one. The transcript won't help him, because he can't read English. And his son is with him, who does speak and read English, but, of course, he can't discuss the testimony he's giving with anybody. In theory, I suppose he could be provided with the audiotapes, but it's really -- as I say, we've been -- we can't speak to him, any more than the Defence can. He has asked VWS, and they've asked us, so I'm putting it before Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I don't suppose he volunteered to them as to why he wanted to have access to the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not that we've been told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner and Mr. Zecevic. Having had the benefit of the advice from the Registry, we are advised that the normal procedure of the transcripts being available only after a five-day interval to allow for such corrections as counsel recognise ought to be made before it is published, after which it is then publicly available, there being no reason which was advanced or volunteered to VWS from the witness requesting it as to why he wanted it, we see no reason to deviate from the established practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, please have a look at tab 59. Document 1D031733 is the number, tab 59. In your set of documents, let me just point the following out: If you have a look at tab 59, the last two pages are page 1 and 3. It's not in the correct order.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's the first page, so just take it out and put it where it should be. [In English] Ms. Usher, the last two pages of the document under tab 59 are the pages 1 and 3, and for some reason it has been -- if you can bring me here, I will do that in a second, please. Thank you very much. I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm sorry, Your Honours. The problem arose because it was up-loaded in e-court with the wrong pagination. But we have resolved the problem in the e-court, but unfortunately failed to resolve it with the binder. I'm sorry for the interruption. [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, this document is a report on crimes in the area of the Banja Luka SJB for the period of the 1st of January until the 20th of December, 1992. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's signed on page 7, the last page, it's signed by the head of the department, Zoran Josic. He's the head of the CID in your SJB of the crime police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date of the document is the 20th of December, 1992. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the first page, it says the purpose of the report is to show that there are problems, since very serious crimes are concerned. This is on page 1 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says since the crimes concerned are extremely serious, and the number of violent crimes has significantly increased with regard to the same period "last year," well, at the beginning of your testimony you said that in 1992, if I remember this correctly, there were 1.000 more crimes than were recorded in 1991; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the third paragraph on page 1, it also says that a total of 107 various crimes were recorded, 90 of which were clarified or identified. And in the case of 90 violent crimes, 101 individuals were involved. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the number 101 individuals. Where is that? Yes, I can see that now. It's the following paragraph. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's page 2 in the English version. You can see that it says that of the 101 individuals, 12 were under age and there were 4 who had repeated their criminal offences; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says that 54 individuals were given three days' detention for the crimes committed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of the Serbian - it's page 3 in the English version in the e-court system - we have a table, and the title is "Ethnic Composition," the type of violent crimes. It says "Murder," "Rape," "Attempted Murder," and so on and so forth, various types of serious crime or violent crime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in the top row, the last eight columns concern the ethnic composition or, rather, the identity of the perpetrators and injured parties; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This table clearly demonstrates that the greatest number of perpetrators and injured parties were to be found amongst the Serbs; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we have a look at the bottom, the last row, if we have a look at the total there, we can see that with regard to all crimes, in 74 cases the perpetrators were Serbs; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you have a look at the table, if you have a look at the last row, where it says "Total" --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- this shows that in 74 cases of violent crimes, the perpetrators were Serbs; in 69 cases, the Serbs were the injured parties?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Croats were concerned, there were 8 Croatian perpetrators and 16 injured parties; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Muslims are concerned, in 19 cases the perpetrators were Muslims, and in 20 they were injured parties; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the same page, the last paragraph, there's an analysis that I think is very important. I think it's on the following page in the English version, on page 4, and it says when one considers the ethnicity of the perpetrators and victims, one can say it is a reflection of the ethnic composition of the population in the territory of Banja Luka municipality. Despite the escalation of the inter-ethnic strife in the Banja Luka municipality in 1992, it was not, and I emphasise "not," usual for members of different ethnic groups to come into conflict. The perpetrators and victims are most frequently of the same ethnicity, and because of their number they're mostly Serbs. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This conclusion drafted by the head of your crime police, Mr. Zoran Josic, the head of the department, is this a conclusion that you agree with?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now just to mention the percentages. It says out of 101 perpetrators, 74 or 73 per cent are of Serbian nationality, 8 of them or 8 per cent are Croatian nationality, and 19 persons or 19 per cent are of Muslim ethnicity. And then it says the situation is similar in the case of the victims of the violent crimes committed. Out of a total of 122 victims: 69 victims, or 58 per cent, were Serbs; 60 victims, or 14 per cent, were Croats; and 25 victims, or 20 per cent, were Muslims. It should be noted that the nationality of eight victims found in Karano [phoen] in 1992 was not established. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, before this report was sent out from the SJB, you, as chief, were made aware of these facts; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. I was the one who requested that this report be drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you saw this report, and you believe that it realistically and correctly reflects the situation as it existed in the territory of your Public Security Station in relation to violent crimes committed in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not a single reason to doubt the accuracy of this data.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the following page, paragraph 7 from the beginning of the document, and I think it's the next page in the B/C/S, and most likely the following page in the English as well, which should be page 5, it says inter-ethnic murders were rare in 1992, even though in the larger part of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there is an inter-ethnic war going on. So far, there have been observed and identified six such cases. In three of them, Serbs killed a total of eight Muslims. In two cases, Muslims killed a total of four Serbs. And in one case, a Croat killed a Serb. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 6 in the English text - I am just being told. I apologise for that - the second paragraph which says: "Cases of murder along inter-ethnic lines ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: According to your recollection, is this information accurate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the end of that page, there is an overview of unresolved murders, that is to say, murders or perpetrators were not found; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in parenthesis it says that there were 12 such murders and that two attempts were also unresolved; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And under item 1, we see that the one of the unresolved murders was that of Zabic, Mirsad. And then under item 4 on the following page, we see it was the murder of Ismet Havic. And then under item 6, an eight-year-old child was killed, Suljo Culum. And then under item 10, it was a married couple, Salihovic, Serif and Fatah. And then under item 11, it was Ibrisagic, Sadeta, and so on. Based on these persons' last names, we can conclude that these are people of Muslim ethnicity; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in this analysis, your chief of department, on page 5 of the Serbian text, states which were the most important causes. I think that's page 7 in the English text.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page in our text, in our version?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's page 5 in the Serbian, and I think it's page 8 -- or, rather, 9 in the English text. In English, it's probably page 10. At any rate, this document says in bullet points that the most important cause for such a situation is certainly politics and wartime events in our country, as a result of which more people have access to fire-arms and explosives devices. And then the second bullet point lists objective factors as causes, subjective factors which are the result of various psychological frustrations because of the war, wartime psychosis, a feeling of insecurity, which leads to increased alcohol consumption. And then they go on to say: "The fact that a large number of people possess fire-arms ..." And let me paraphrase, that due to increased alcohol consumption, this leads to conflicts which break out, and it frequently happens that for reasons of insignificant and banal circumstances, people are killed; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your chief of department, in his analysis, says that in almost 60 per cent of the cases, the perpetrator and the victims, well, were under the influence of alcohol, and that the murder or bodily injury inflicted had no significant deep motive; for example, personal benefit, hatred, and so on, but that, rather, in most cases it was a matter of fierce conflict which resulted in murder or injury. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- did you agree at the time with the analysis of causes, as it was written down by your chief, causes for murders and violent crime, in the territory of SJB Banja Luka in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this analysis stems from analysing causes and methods of how the crime was perpetrated, and I have no reasons to question it or to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then the report, at the end of this page, in the last sentence, I think, they say: "It is estimated that almost 50 per cent of violent crime is related to the army, either directly that they are the perpetrators or indirectly (that they provide weapons, leave it without supervision)," and so on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's the last sentence in the Serbian text on that page, page 11 in the English text.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that in accordance with your recollections, that that's how it was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here it is estimated, so most likely it was a result of the analysis conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We will look at that analysis in the following page of the English text on page 6, where they say: "This statement can be supported by the fact that in the course of 1992, members of the army carried out 38 violent crimes, which is 35.5 per cent or one-third of total crime." And then they give what kind of crimes were committed by members of the army: murders, attempted murders, involuntary manslaughter, and serious bodily injury; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In page 6 of the Serbian text, which is the following page in the English text, I think page 11, they say that SJB Banja Luka observed, in a timely manner, that there was an increase in violent crime, and that in order to decrease it, and to resolve crimes, and identify perpetrators, they undertook preventive and repressive measures and actions. Do you see where they say that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then in item 1, where they elaborate on this, they say that they were working more intensely in order to discover and confiscate illegally-obtained weapons and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then under item 5, they say that when issuing fire-arms permits, SJB Banja Luka will bear in mind this increase in crime and will revoke fire-arms licenses in cases where it is justified based on the law?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's on the following page, I think. We will go back to this issue a bit later, this confiscation of legally-owned weapons for which there is a permit, because my learned friend Ms. Korner put a question to you about it. And to conclude, at the very end, on page 7, your chief of department says it is realistic to expect that this increase will continue, because the experience from war in neighbouring countries confirms that. Here they mean an increase in violent crime; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In order to document this that is mentioned in your report, dated 20th of December, 1992, I will now show you a report from your SJB from the 25th of May, 1993, which is tab 116. The document is 1D002270.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said "116"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document pertains only to a crime of murder, however, and not to all other violent crime; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 25th of May, 1993, and it is also signed by your chief of department, Zoran Josic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1993 -- I apologise. This document relates to 1992 and the first five months of 1993. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then in this document, they state that a total of 84 crimes were committed during that period of time and that there were a total of 105 victims. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Once again, they conduct an analysis of the ethnic background of victims, and they say that the Serbs represent the majority or 46 per cent of all victims?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forty-eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, it's 46 per cent of all victims, which is 48 persons. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 18 per cent of the victims were Croats, 28 per cent of them were Muslims, and the others were 8 per cent; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then further on in the text, they list by name all victims from 1992 and the first five months of 1993. They give their full names, years of birth, and they also classified based on their ethnic background; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the very end, there are nine victims whose ethnic background was not established. They are in the category of "Others"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy and veracity of this data?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please turn to tab 114, 1D002134. This a document with the subject "Information," which you signed on the 30th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This information was sent to the Municipal Assembly or, rather, to the president of the executive board; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By law, we were duty-bound to inform them whenever they requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this pertains to confiscation of legal and illegal weapons from citizens in the period between the 1st of January, 1992, until the 21st of September, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document, we see that it is headed "Information," and in paragraph 2 you say: "In accordance or based on the security situation and the conclusion of the War Presidency, Banja Luka SJB is taking all the necessary measures in order to disarm the residents." And then they go on to say that the basic task is to collect and check by means of implementation of adequate operational and tactical activities, and to implement all intelligence on illegal acquisition and possession of fire-arms in order to improve the security situation in Banja Luka municipality. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you still consider that these activities, aimed at confiscating illegal and legal fire-arms from citizens in 1992, were aimed at improving the security situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it was, and that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was there any other reason for doing that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, which is page 3 of the document, which is probably page 4 in the English version, it is stated in the period between the 1st of January, 1992, and the 21st of September, 1992, 180 misdemeanor reports were filed against persons who were illegally arming themselves. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, it is stated that 43 criminal reports were filed for illegal possession of weapons and explosive devices, under Article 213 of the Criminal Code of Bosnia-Herzegovina, against 58 individuals. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of the Serbian version, and we're good as far as the English version is concerned, it is stated that of 58 individuals, 25.9 per cent were Serbs -- or, rather, 15, 16 Croats, and 24 were Muslims, or, rather, 41.4 per cent of Muslims. These were individuals against whom criminal reports were filed for illegal possession of weapons or explosives; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, in paragraph 4 it is stated: "In accordance with the conclusions of the Banja Luka Municipal War Presidency, and in keeping with the provisions of Article 28 on the Law on Acquisition, Possession, and Carrying of Weapons, the Banja Luka Public Security Station has confiscated 1.012 pieces of fire-arms from the citizens who did not have a weapons permit issued by the authorised body." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I think that this is a convenient moment, now that we have broached the subject, for you to explain the following: In keeping with the Law on the Acquisition, Possession, and Carrying of Weapons, the citizens of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who wanted to obtain a hunting rifle for hunting purposes, or for purposes of their own safety, would approach the relevant public security station with a request to be given a permit for the purchase of a piece of weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Once in receipt of the request, the public security station, in the territory of which the citizen resides, would vet the citizen, would it not, would engage in checking the citizen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The vetting procedure would include the verification of any criminal files. Did it involve anything else?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, operative and field vetting as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what operative vetting and what field vetting stand for?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under "operative vetting," the individual who is being checked may have been the subject of an investigation or a suspect, but the case never reached a court having jurisdiction. Still, such individuals would be kept in operative records. The "field vetting" required policemen to go out into the field and check what sort of character the individual had, whether he was prone to drinking, or brawls, or rows with neighbours, et cetera, in order to establish whether such a person was, in fact, a suitable individual to carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The field vetting would be conducted in the following manner, would it not: A policeman from the area where the individual seeking to buy a weapon resides would go to the locality where the individual resides and talk to the neighbours and persons knowing the individual?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, there was a form which had to be filled in by the policemen and which would be conclusive in terms of establishment whether the individual was suitable for -- suitable to be issued with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, an individual who had not been -- who did not have a criminal record, had not been convicted, had not been on any of the operative records, and the field vetting of whom had shown that he was not prone to violence, such an individual would be given a permit for the purchase of weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, if the individual wanted to buy a hunting rifle, he also had to give proof of his membership of a hunting society.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, is it not, that once the SJB would issue its clearance, the individual could go and purchase the sort of weapon for which that particular permit was related to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would be given two copies of the permit, and one copy would be kept by the store where the weapon is purchased, and the other copy was to be kept by the citizen together with the invoice showing where the weapon was purchased, which was needed for the weapon to be registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Once the individual gains possession of a piece of weapon, once he buys it in a store, he has to go back to the SJB, where a weapons license or weapons certificate would be issued to him, would it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the certificate contained the name of the person, type of weapon, calibre, and year of manufacture of the weapon to which the certificate referred; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, based on the competence mentioned herein under Article 28 of the Law on the Acquisition, Possession, and Carrying of Weapons, the SJB had at all times the power under the law to withdraw any -- or revoke any permit it may have issued to an individual in respect of a piece of weapon that the individual is in possession of; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had that sort of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This sort of power would be exercised by the SJB in a situation where, let's say, an individual has been issued with a permit and has purchased a piece of weaponry, and subsequently his spouse has reported violent behaviour of that individual. Thereupon, in accordance with the powers you had and in accordance with the procedures that was in place, the SJB would seize the weapon from the individual, would it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We rigorously applied or exercised our power to confiscate weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The same situation applied to the power under Article 28 throughout the year 1992. I mean, in other words, you had that power throughout 1992, and you did resort to it in order to improve the security situation in the Banja Luka area. This was the sole reason, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the very end of the document, the last three pages in Serbian contain a list of individuals against whom criminal reports were filed, stating their ethnicity, year of birth, address, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
