utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I would like to quickly go through a series of orders and dispatches issued by the Ministry of the Interior and copied or sent to you. That's behind tab 7, 65 ter 87.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Number 7, tab 7. This is the document bearing the date of the 17th of April, 1992, signed by an individual on behalf of Minister Stanisic, the minister of the interior. The document was sent to all the security services centres in Republika Srpska and relates to recorded cases of unlawful possession of movable and immovable property committed on the part of certain members of the service. The minister, and this is back on the 17th of April, 1992, orders that the strictest of measures should be applied against such individuals. In brackets, it states "dismissal, criminal prosecution," et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph, it is stated, similarly, it has been noted that a number of individuals prone to crime had been committing theft of socially-owned and public property in an organised fashion, and that these should be brought to justice. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Lastly, the minister assigns chiefs of sectors and chiefs -- or, rather, chiefs of centres and chiefs of public security stations as responsible for the implementation of these measures; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving such a document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look behind number 9, which is P553, dated the 29th of April. It's a dispatch from the Security Services Centre. The date is the 29th of April, 1992. It's a dispatch by Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, the CSB chief, wherein he forwards, in its entirety, the letter from the minister of the interior, does he not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I haven't read through the documents, but I have no reason to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The dispatch reads: "We received from the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sarajevo, a dispatch, the contents of which we bring here in its entirety." And this is the number that is stated here that shows that it's the same letter, is it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness be shown 1D58. That's number 25 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is an order by Minister Mico Stanisic, dated the 23rd of July, 1992, wherein it is stated all the members of the MUP who have committed crime should have legal measures taken against them, should be removed from "our ranks," dismissed, and made available to the Army of the Serbian Republic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Chief of administration at the headquarters, commanders of police units, and chiefs of security centres are responsible for implementing the order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving such a dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several such dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll show another document, and then -- I'll list them for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. 1D166, tab 53, it's a series of dispatches that Minister Stanisic sent in relation to the same issue. 53, 1D176, this is an order from the minister of the interior, dated the 27th of July. That's four days after the previous one. Item 2 says: "In accordance with my order dated the 23rd of July," that's the one we had a look at a minute ago, "I hereby order that certain individuals be removed immediately from the ministry who were held criminally responsible ..." And so on and so forth. So you can see that this reproduces the dispatch dated the 23rd of July, more or less; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 4 says that all special units formed in the course of the war in the territory of CSB should be disbanded and placed under the command of the Army of the Serbian Republic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you received this dispatch from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this dispatch, but I remember the order. I had it in my hands at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, it's tab 54, P592, and this is the very same order. It has to do with the same problem. The date is the 29th of July, 1992. And there's another order dated the 24th of July, 1992. 1D59 is the number, and it's tab 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you said that you saw a number of such orders -- that you received a number of such orders, this shows that as early as the 17th of April, and up until the end of July and later, these orders from the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska are repeated. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you a different type of order now. Tab 34, 65 ter 222. In fact, I apologise. Tab 35, P655. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's an order dated the 19th of August, 1992, in which the chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin, forwards to all SJBs -- I assume you received it. Well, it says it's an order from the minister of the interior of the Serbian Republic, dated the 10th of August, and a dispatch that deals with the same issue, dated the 17th of August. And then it says -- or, rather, a certain text is reproduced that was provided by the Ministry of the Interior to the CSB. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having received this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but there's no reason for me to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: P665, 65 ter 223. In the e-court system, it's a different document, not the one we are commenting on. I apologise. It's 605, P605. I do apologise, 65 ter 223. Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it. I'm sure I received it. There's no reason why I shouldn't have received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This has to do with an instruction or an order from the minister, according to which preventive detention should be applied in accordance with the rules in force. Custody and detention measures should be taken only within the scope of the regulations in force. And it says hygiene and health conditions on prison premises should satisfy basic standards. It says: "You are responsible for the lines of individuals, and no abuse is permitted." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really decipher the last sentence. Yes, I've found it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 1, do you agree that that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under item 2, it says: "The Serbian Army is directly responsible for the security of collection centres." And so on. And then if they don't have enough manpower to perform this work, it is necessary for wartime assignments to be allotted. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This concerns the police reserve force that is re-subordinated to the army for a certain task; isn't that correct? That's what the minister has in mind?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that last sentence and your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that when the minister says if they don't have sufficient manpower to perform their work, he has the Serbian Army in mind, provide wartime assignments, and he has the police in mind; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What does it mean, if they're given wartime assignments? It means that they're being re-subordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that this concerns members of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, these same orders are under -- the orders that have to do with the same problems, we have one dated the 20th of August, 1992, and it's under number P606, tab 36. And then we have the same order about the same problem, 1D57 is the number, dated the 24th of August, 1992, and it is under tab 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please, let's have a look at the document under tab 50, 1D000509.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, before you move on to the document, perhaps we could take the break at this point. It's 5.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you very much. I lost track of the time. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back to the stand, the Chamber, having received a motion from the Office of the Prosecution to amend its 65 ter list, the Chamber would be grateful for expedited responses from the Defence by Monday. Thank you. Orally, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, can I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honours, just for the transcript, it was brought to our attention that there was a mistake on page 42, line 18. In fact, it should say -- the whole sentence: "The Banja Luka Public Security Station has confiscated 1.012 pieces of fire-arms from the citizens who did not have a weapons permit issued by the authorised body." This is not correct, because the document says who did have a weapons permit issued by the authorised body. But in all fairness to the interpreters, we found that the English translation of the 1D235 actually contains "did not," so we are going to file for the revised translation and then re-admit it into the e-court. I'm just putting this on the record because of the transcript. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So noted, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, had you an intervention?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll wait [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, have a look at tab 29, document 1D85. It's tab 29. This is a dispatch from the Banja Luka CSB, dated the 8th of June, 1992: "To all public security stations - to the chief." That should include you, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the head of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin. You can see it in the lower left-hand corner, can't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in this dispatch, the chief of the Banja Luka CSB reproduces the entire text of the dispatch that he received from the Ministry of the Interior, which was signed by the assistant of the minister for crime prevention and detection, Dobro Planojecic. And Mr. Zupljanin says that all authorised officials of the SJB must be informed of the contents of the dispatch and they must abide by the instructions in the dispatch. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The original dispatch from the ministry is 1D84. That's for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. Mr. Tutus, do you remember having received this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that in the order it says that there has been a significant increase in crimes, especially in war crimes? Do you remember that part of the order? It's the first sentence in the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere in the middle, the order says particular attention should be paid to the detection of the perpetrators of war crimes, to the documenting of crimes committed by groups and individuals, and to their capture and apprehension, or, rather, surrender to the appropriate authorities. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the assistant minister, Dobro Planojevic, the assistant minister for crime prevention and detection, sent this on the 8th of June, 1992. Did you know Mr. Dobro Planojevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did the Banja Luka SJB abide by the instructions of this dispatch in accordance with the order from the centre's chief?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, there's another document that deals with the same subject. It's under tab 129. 1D63 is the document number. This is a dispatch, instructions, dated the 19th of July, 1992, forwarded to all SJBs, CSBs, in fact, and Mico Stanisic signed the document. Paragraph 2 says: "A questionnaire will be completed at security services centres for all persons, regardless of their ethnicity (Muslims, Croats, Serbs, and others) against whom criminal reports have been submitted ...", because there is reasonable grounds to suspect that they have committed certain crimes, war crimes, what one has in mind." Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this. It wasn't addressed to SJBs, public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I'm certain that the CSB informed you of the instructions and of the questionnaire that related to war crimes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a few more documents that I would like to deal with. Mr. Tutus, I know that this must be tiring for you, but unfortunately it's necessary. Document 119. 1D52 is the document number. This is a mandatory instruction on the procedure of the Ministry of the Interior in performance of searchs and pursuits from October 1992. It says "Bijeljina," which is where the ministry had its seat at the time. It was in Bijeljina; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that the ministry had its seat in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this mandatory instruction? It has the signature of Minister Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the signature. So I suppose we received it, but I cannot remember it specifically now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have just one question concerning this mandatory instruction. It has already been admitted into evidence in this case. On page 2, under item 1, it says that: "Search and pursuit activities within the meaning of these instructions shall constitute a system of operational, tactical, and technical measures taken by internal affairs organs in order to discover certain persons or items connected to a crime, and dead bodies ." Do you agree with this definition of search and pursued activities?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that these mandatory instructions were sent to all SJBs and to all subjects within the Ministry of the Interior precisely in order to uncover the perpetrators of crimes; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these instructions specify what steps need to be taken within search and pursuit activities, and there was no reason for us not to receive these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. I will show you another instructions, which is tab 136, 1D51. I'm showing you this because with my learned friend, you commented upon the issue of reporting. So we now need tab 136, 1D51.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have 35 -- 135.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It should be the last document in the binder with yellow --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was added subsequently. You remember that you and Ms. Korner made some comments about reporting, and you said, in answer to one of the questions she put to you - I can't give you the exact reference, but I assume you will remember - that you said that you made your reports in accordance with the instructions which were in force in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the time when you entered on duty, and that you provided reports in accordance with those instructions with that document. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you see the instructions here. You see that there are several kinds of reporting, urgent, current, periodical and statistical reports, and that this was issued by the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, with the seat in Bijeljina in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive these instructions, and did you act in accordance with them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We most likely received it, and we acted in accordance with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. The last instructions I wish to show you is in tab 132; 1D54, tab 132. These are the instructions issued by the minister of the interior concerning disciplinary responsibility from the 19th of September, 1992. And in paragraph 2 -- or, rather, on the first page, it says that these rules on the disciplinary responsibility of workers, during an immediate threat of war and during a state of war, it now envisages a summary procedure for establishing the disciplinary responsibility of the workers of MUP. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And on the last page, which is page 5, page 5 of the Serbian text, in Article 17, which should be the penultimate and ultimate page in the English text -- so in Article 17, it says that statute of limitations is extended, the deadlines are extended?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It specifies the statute of limitation and the time-periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You must have been familiar with these instructions and with the rules on the disciplinary responsibility of the workers of the Ministry of the Interior in the state of war and immediate threat of war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to illustrate that by using a practical example, I will remind you by saying that in your interview, I think you said that in the course of 1992 - I think that's on page 80 of your interview - you filed one or two -- you instituted one or two disciplinary procedures against some of the MUP workers. In one of the cases, there was -- there were allegations of confiscation of coffee, and in the other case, it involved Gagula, Ivica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, but I don't think we had only two cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how many cases do you think there were, according to your recollection? How many times did you institute disciplinary proceedings in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now, but I'm sure that there were more cases. I mentioned Gagula just as an illustration, and also the coffee case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. I wanted to show you this document involving Gagula precisely in order to explain to the Trial Chamber how this procedure for establishing disciplinary responsibility was regulated. Could we now please see tab 121, which is P1039. See here, this is a letter from the Disciplinary Committee of Banja Luka, signed by the secretary of the Disciplinary Committee, Aleksandar Jovicic. Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not Jovcic, it's Jovicic. An I is missing after V.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is dated the 20th of August, 1992. It says here that the disciplinary prosecutor, Rodic, Radomir, was from the Banja Luka SJB. Do you know this person? Did he really work there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise. I may be wrong with Jovicic's last name. I'm not sure whether it's Jovicic or Jovcic. I don't want to the claim that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but it's not essential for our purposes. You know Radomir Rodic? I asked you if you know the person.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says here: "Subject, Ivica Gagula, disciplinary responsibility." And then it says here: "We enclose a letter with the initiative of the SJB Banja Luka to institute proceedings aimed at establishing disciplinary responsibility of Ivica Gagula." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this case of Ivica Gagula?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that there were proceedings, but I can't remember the details. Perhaps I need to read this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Aleksandar Jovicic says in this document that no longer than within three days from the date of receipt of this initiative, you need to, "you" meaning Radomir Rodic, you, as the disciplinary prosecutor, need to write a decision on temporary suspension of this worker from work and request to institute proceedings in order to establish disciplinary responsibility, signed by chief of the Banja Luka CSB. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this temporary removal from work is actually a suspension?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now please look at tab 123, which is 65 ter 1459. Tab 123, 65 ter 1452. Tab 123.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have it. I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'm saying this just for the sake of the transcript, and other people who are listening, so that they have an accurate reference. This document is dated 24th of August, 1992. This is a request to initiating proceedings for establishing disciplinary responsibility. And then on page 2, you see that it is signed by Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the centre, and then there's a stamp there as well. And this request pertains to Ivica Gagula; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the proposal on page 1, on the first page of the document, where it says: "I propose ...," it says -- rather, Mr. Zupljanin, chief of the centre, proposes that a hearing be held before the Disciplinary Committee, to which the accused, Ivica Gagula, should be invited, witnesses, and the prosecutor, Rodic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document? Do you know of its contents?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is tab 124, which is 65 ter 1453, from the 7th of October, 1992. It says that this is from the Banja Luka CSB, the Third Disciplinary Board, and this is a record of the main hearing or, rather, a record of the hearing held on the 7th of October, 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on the preamble, we can see that this involves proceedings against Ivica Gagula for grave violation of work duty?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it says who was present: President of the Disciplinary Board, then two members, then the disciplinary prosecutor, the accused, and witnesses; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then finally at page 7 and 8 of the Serbian text, I suppose penultimate and ultimate page in the English text, it says what the decision of the Disciplinary Board was. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During the proceedings, the Disciplinary Board established that the accused, Ivica Gagula, was indeed responsible for this grave violation. We don't need to go into details. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And a disciplinary measure was handed down that he was to change his work for a period of six months. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this change of work-place for a period of six months must have meant that he was demoted?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which necessarily involved reduction in pay and the like?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and most likely he no longer had his official authorities during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D237, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now let's have a look at the last document, the last one I want to show you today, tab 125, document 65 ter 1454. This is a written decision, a copy of the decision, dated the 17th of October, 1992. It is the Disciplinary Commission that is forwarding its decision on Ivica Gagula. And it repeats the decision that it took at the hearing held on the 7th of October; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on page 2, it says -- or there's a statement of reasons. The Disciplinary Commission has determined that he, in fact, violated his work obligations, and it says on what basis this was determined. And it says something about the legal remedy. It says against this decision -- it's possible to appeal against this decision by filing the appeal with the minister of the interior three days after -- or within three days from the date on which the decision was received. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if the appeal is filed in a timely manner, this postpones the effect of the decision, and it's been signed by the president of the board. Can you see that, there's a stamp and a signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It also says it was forwarded to certain individuals. It says it was forwarded to the employee who was named, the person who can appeal, it was forwarded to the minister, to you, the chief of the SJB - you initiated the proceedings - it is official for employment relationships to the Disciplinary Commission, the disciplinary prosecutor, and to the archives; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in this decision -- I apologise. I'm going a little too fast again. It's on the basis of this decision that the first-level proceedings, disciplinary proceedings, were completed against an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, an employee of yours in the SJB, Gagula, Ivica, and this was done in accordance with the law; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now Ivica Gagula had three days to file an appeal to the minister, as the second-level court or second-level instance?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D203 [sic], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The record is not correct, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the transcript, Your Honours, this is Exhibit 1D238. Thank you for noticing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since we are dealing with disciplinary responsibility, I have the impression that in your interview you mentioned the case of Pero Tanjanovic [phoen]. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petar Tanazovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Petar Tanazovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Petar Tanazovic was the commander of the Medan Police Station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And at one point in time, if I remember this correctly, Mr. Tanazovic committed one or two crimes, the crime of murder, and subsequently after the proceedings instituted against him, the proceedings for murder, it was discovered that he had committed the crime of rape, he had raped a lady of Croatian nationality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. We had such information, the case was processed, but I'm not sure whether we had sufficient evidence and whether we filed a report against him on that basis. I don't know whether there was sufficient evidence to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Tanazovic committed the crime of murder at a check-point where he opened fire on members of the Territorial Defence, I think, or the police. I'm not sure. He opened fire on a Serb and a Muslim at that check-point, on which occasion the Serb died; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a mixed police check-point. It was manned by policemen of various ethnicity. He arrived in an intoxicated state, and it is true that he killed a Serb whose surname I believe was Kovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And as a result of having committed that crime, criminal proceedings were naturally instituted against him?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That very same evening, he was arrested. I arrived in the SJB that evening. I saw the state he was in. We placed him in detention for a three-day period immediately and then referred him to the relevant judiciary authorities. And he was convicted for that crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, disciplinary proceedings were instituted against him which were different from the criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details, but his employment was, in any event, terminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I just have a few more questions for you. Do you know someone called Predrag Radulovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Radulovic, Predrag Radulovic, was an employee of the State Security Service, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: An employee of the State Security Service. Later, it was called the National Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Banja Luka CSB or --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the armed conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina, he was a member of the State Security Service within the Republican Secretariat for Internal Affairs. And, similarly, prior to the armed conflict he was transferred to Banja Luka, and he worked for the State Security Service in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever ask Mr. Radulovic to provide you with certain information relating to any events he might have been familiar with or any events with regard to which he had information as a result of the work he was involved in?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never asked for such information. I didn't have the right to do so. If I had done that, that would have been in violation of the rules in force, so I couldn't have asked for such information and I certainly didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say this, what I'm interested in is whether you perhaps had a certain type of private relationship on the basis of which you could ask him for such information on a private basis. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't do that, and I wouldn't have allowed myself to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did Predrag Radulovic ever provide you certain data and information on his own initiative, and did he ever ask you to forward such data and information to the minister, Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would have been a case of abuse if I had done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you again whether, when you had personal contact with him, he provided you with certain information and asked you to inform Minister Mico Stanisic about that information, or anyone else in an executive position in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never made such a request. Had we met in the corridor, I wouldn't exclude that possibility, but I don't remember him having conveyed any information to me. I certainly don't remember this having happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether he asked you to forward certain information he provided you with to Minister Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a certain sense, I have answered that question. No one asked me to do that. No one could have asked me to do that. I had no authority to act in such a way, and I wouldn't have accepted to act in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions, and I do apologise for having tired you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Mr. Tutus.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since it's no longer -- my name is Mr. Krgovic. I represent Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, and I will be cross-examining you for the remainder of the day. Since you may already be quite tired, since we've been here for a while, if you feel tired, please tell me. Perhaps we could adjourn a little earlier today, if you're feeling tired. I've prepared a binder for you. Could the usher please assist me and provide the witness with this binder. It contains the documents I will be using in the course of my cross-examination, and you will find the relevant documents under tab numbers. This will make it easier for you to follow. Mr. Tutus, when answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor and my colleague Mr. Zecevic, you spoke about the events that preceded the wartime period in the area of Banja Luka, and you spoke about your personal dissatisfaction and the dissatisfaction of your colleagues with the situation in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and, in particular, with the situation in the area of the SJB that you were in. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll briefly summarise some of the subjects that were dealt with and some of the reasons for which you and members of the MUP were dissatisfied. In 1991, in the border-line areas of Banja Luka, in the marginal areas of Banja Luka that were part of the -- or that came under the Banja Luka CSB - I'm referring to the municipalities that border with Croatia - in those areas the security situation deteriorated; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise? Where did this deteriorate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the territory of those border-line areas, the security situation deteriorated before the war broke out. I have Bosanska Gradiska and Bosanski Novi in mind and all those areas that border with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't assess the security situation in areas covered by other SJBs. But if you are asking me whether there were any incidents in those areas, yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as for the situation in Croatia, the war there, and the situation in these border-line municipalities, these situations also affected the security situation in Banja Luka; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So first many refugees arrived from Croatia, 10.000 or 15.000 at the time. That was towards the end of 1991 and at the beginning of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that significantly influenced the way in which the security situation deteriorated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as a result, the population moved from those marginal municipalities. They would go to Banja Luka -- they would move to Banja Luka because they were afraid and they felt safer in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's possible, but I don't have any official information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, given the number of armed individuals increased and they were members of various formations, as a result of this public law and order was disrupted in the area of Banja Luka; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The increase in the number of armed citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The increase in the number of armed citizens resulted in significant disruption of public law and order. Fire would be opened, and these individuals would cause certain incidents?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't just disrupt public law and order, but they also committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So I'll now show you a document about this subject. Number 1, 2D -- 2D0207 -- 2D0020705. It's under tab 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 30th of September, 1991. It's from the CSB. It has "Information on the Security Situation in the Territory of the Centre."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to the minister and deputy minister?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the signature and the stamp?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "Chief of the Centre, Stojan Zupljanin."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's his signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the second page of this document, the last paragraph. It says there that in parallel with the intensification of armed attacks from the territory of Croatia against the aforesaid municipalities and other municipalities covered by the centre, there has also been an escalation of sabotage terrorist operations which, together with numerous other serious security implications, is primarily serving to bring about a climate of foreign and widespread armed inter-ethnic conflict. And then they mention that there were 15 blatant sabotage terrorist acts and so on. When a chief compiles such reports, he would normally receive information from you as to the security situation in the jurisdiction of your station; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever he asked from us, we would provide him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you turn to the next page, it says there that explosives were launched, bombs were activated, hand-grenades thrown at residences and cafes and catering establishments?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where are you reading this from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the next page, the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it describes the situation as it was on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at the last page, where the signature was, and there is a statement by the chief. And he says that more and more frequent shooting at night by unidentified individuals and groups at night-time in ethnically-mixed areas is causing the very dangerous further heightening of inter-ethnic relations and imminent risks, and so on. Do you agree that this all led to such a situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think this document has been admitted into evidence yet. So if there are no objections, could that be done now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D54, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When answering questions during the your testimony, and also in your interview, I think, you said that you were dissatisfied with the situation, both financially and in terms of the equipment, the situation as it was at the public security stations?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And especially if one bears in mind all of these circumstances that you mentioned, this significantly made your work harder and made it more difficult to be efficient at the Banja Luka SJB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the state of equipment and resources definitely affect the work of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And given the increase in the number of incidents, you certainly must have required an increase in staff members, policemen, who could have dealt with this situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now please look at 2D38, tab 2 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you said in your interview that you addressed all relevant instances in order to resolve this question and to highlight how serious the situation was in the territory of Banja Luka. You said that letters were being sent to various persons. Please look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, let us go back to the first page. So the second paragraph from the bottom, it says: "Our dispatch 11227, dated 26th of August, 1991, by way of it I sent to the relevant republic organs observations and complaints concerning the number of police workers according to the job description scheme, where it says that we were discriminated in relation to other centres." So it says that you were in a worse position than other stations?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that specifically. But now that I'm looking at this document, I think that you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So then it says that -- on the second page of this document, they make an analysis, and they say that you need to have 11 workers, 11 policemen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that there was a problem with employing persons, that consents for employing somebody were late, and that you also had problems in this schematic, giving job descriptions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And all of this together caused you to distrust, you and your other colleagues --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's in the evidence now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. That's the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Tutus, but the English translation of this document does not correspond to the original. So now we have the right one. This is when you voiced your discontent in that meeting. That was just one of the illustrations of problems that you faced at the time for which there was no understanding within the ranks of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, can we please look at the next document, tab 3, 2D040140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, if I'm not mistaken, this document, the previous one, is MFI'd. You want to keep it that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I think that it was admitted by -- when the witness who identified it, whose name I don't want to mention -- we're in public session. When that witness testified, we admitted it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested only in the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, Madam Registrar tells me that it is still MFI'd. We suppose you're confusing somewhere. But to me, it was still MFI'd, and the Registrar confirms that it was still MFI'd. I just want to be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, since the witness recognised the document and its contents, then if there are no objections, why don't we resolve that confusion now? [In English] The witness which I cross-examined recognised the signature on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay, all right, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So it's now exhibited, marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Tutus. We had an administrative confusion to settle. Now, as a result of deterioration of the security situation on the ground, the federal minister, Gracanin, came to visit Banja Luka in 1991. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So they mentioned the working visit to the centre and the persons who attended that meeting. You were among them, among the attendees?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was a publicly-announced visit, there were no secrets. Minister Delimustafic was present, as we can see from this letter; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no secret meeting held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because we have heard from some other witnesses that this was an almost secret visit, that it was organised and -- organised under the auspices of Stojan Zupljanin. You don't think so, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was a secret meeting. I think it was reported on by the media. I can't remember, really, but I don't see why it would have been secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from a news report by "Tanjug." This is a brief news agency report. [In English] I don't ask it to be tendered, because there are these newspaper articles. [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, I just wanted to run some things by you in 1991 and early 1992. And now I will go back to events which would be of interest for this Chamber which were in 1992. But before that, I wanted to ask you something about responsibilities, which you touched upon in your examination-in-chief and in your interview, concerning the responsibilities of SJB and CSB. You will agree with me, won't you, that according to the system as it was before the war, an SJB and its scope of work, the scope of work and duties coincided with the jurisdiction of the Basic Municipal Court; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And an SJB, when it comes to criminal cases, would act only in cases for which the Basic Municipal Court had jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the other hand, a CSB was the one who filed charges and who prosecuted cases that fell under the jurisdiction of a higher court, a regional court?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A CSB was authorised to act in cases which came under the jurisdiction of higher courts and also in cases of crimes which were all listed individually in the instructions issued by the secretary of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You are now referring to sabotage acts?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The crimes were listed individually; kidnapping an aircraft, endangering safety, also grave property damage, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this is how it was when the war began in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war broke out in the territory of Banja Luka, the centre, as far as I'm aware, had under its jurisdiction 11 SJBs. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember whether there were 11, but, yes, it had under its jurisdiction these stations that were mentioned in the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And after the conflict broke out and some additional municipalities joined the Autonomous Region of Krajina, that number increased to 26; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Which is almost two and a half times more than previously, before the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure about the ratio, but significantly more, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your examination-in-chief, you spoke about responsibilities, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, if you're about to move on to something else, it's very near 7.00, so we may as well take the break at this point, if you're moving on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention the question of the intercepts? Your Honours admitted them orally and said you would give reasons later. I'm taking that that meant you admitted all the intercepts that we applied to admit through the witness; is that right? Because at the moment, we're having a slight debate with the Registry about whether the intercepts are admitted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we release the witness in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was the 4th of March, 2010, and Judge Hall said: "The Chamber, for reasons which will follow, accedes to the application."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the position is that all of the transcripts have not been admitted, and by Monday, certainly in advance of the Witness Mandic coming to testify, you would be alerted as to which have been admitted and which haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really sorry, but this not our understanding of what you said, and we would have pursued submissions if we'd understood that. You said, in terms: "The Chamber has [indiscernible] motion from the Prosecution in respect of the package of documents to be tendered through the witness whose testimony was completed yesterday, and the Chamber, for reasons which will follow, accedes to the application." And we're now being told that you're not admitting all the exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, there is a slight problem with a few of the -- there is -- we have discovered there is a slight problem with a few of the transcripts that makes it questionable whether we can admit them. And so for the purposes of the evidence offered by Mr. Mandic on Wednesday next week, you'll have to rely on the 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, may I just, in that case, for future reference, make this point: It's the problem with oral rulings like this. We understood, and I believe I'm speaking for all of us, that the ruling was that you admitted everything. Had we known that Your Honours were not going to admit, we would have sought to make oral arguments. As it is, we now don't know, nor do I know for the preparation of, as you put it, Mr. Mandic, what's admitted, and what isn't, and why. Well, Your Honour, obviously, I mean, there's nothing I can say, but may I suggest that in future, that we do not get an oral ruling like that, which leads everybody to believe erroneously that the whole package that we've applied for has been admitted. And if it's not to be admitted, could we be informed so that we can argue the matter? That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I don't know if there's anything that we can usefully add at this point, so we'll take the adjournment to Monday morning, and, unless there is a change, all of our sittings next week are morning sittings in Courtroom 1. Sorry, before we adjourn, Mr. Tutus, I'm obliged to remind you of what I would have said at the first day's adjournment, that you're still under oath and cannot discuss the case with anyone outside of the court or not have any communication with counsel. So I trust that everyone has a safe weekend. Thank you.
